rule.summary: All 36 stored choices (E1..E5 and PLACEBO; final_all65 plus 5 blocks each) match ruling 53 (with ruling 64) when I apply it myself to the stored candidates. All 15 PLACEBO fixed-w block choices match too. I also rebuilt every candidate's mean and SE (324 values) from the assembled stage-B pool tables with an independent Node copy of evalcore's ranking, BLAKE2b-64 tie-break, weighted RRF and numpy's pairwise mean and std(ddof=1). All 324 values are bit-identical to choices.json, and my 36 choices and the block commit lists equal the stored ones. Ruling 57 picks E1: the four-decimal figures are E1 0.2470, E4 0.2463, E3 0.2458, E2 0.2456, E5 0.2455. E1 has no tie at four decimals and leads E4 by 7.196e-4. item27.json says the same: E1, c04, w=1, figure 0.24700985766370384, epochs 70, s=1, device cuda, tie group [E1]. Its per-arm figures and candidate lists equal choices.json and tune.json. Its sha256 file matches. Its tables_digest equals my Node recomputation of ruling 82's digest (f8cb1f8b...). Its 18 code hashes match the current files. I found one latent divergence in evalcore: a NaN embedding score would still get an RRF term. The real data cannot trigger it, because the 45 pool tables hold 0 non-finite scores. No divergence I found changes a stored choice. The held-out run gets E1 (RotatE) c04, w = 1, 70 epochs, seeds 1, 2 and 3, s = 1, on cuda, as the arm alone and fused, plus RRF, PPR, CO and DIR.
